libs.english_description: A Journey to the West mythology MUD from AKAI Studio's Tomud-branded lineage, byte-identical in file layout and bug set to this collection's sibling xyj2006n (down to sharing the same client-detection gate: the first line sent after connecting must be the bare literal "2060", the automatic reply from Tomud/"Smiling Proud Wanderer" clients, or the connection is dropped as illegal). New characters start at a South City Inn and can apprentice into the Lingtai Fangcun Mountain / Three-Star Cave sect under second-generation disciple Guang Yunzi; a gift-giving NPC there hands new arrivals a free starter set of thirteen basic skills.

libs.name: 西游记451
libs.english_description: Journey to the West, from the same ES II mudlib family as this collection's xyj42/xyj2000, sharing their Thirty-Three Heavens / Peach Garden / Penglai map style and Lingtai Fangcun Mountain sect. Registration here has no explicit "new character" keyword -- entering an English ID that isn't already on file goes straight to "Creating a new character named X, are you sure? (y/n)" -- and talent points aren't assigned by adjusting slots but through a reroll loop ("Do you accept these talent values? [n|y|q]"). New characters land at the South City Inn; apprenticing to the sect's senior master correctly fails for outsiders (a real in-code experience-and-Taoism-points gate) but succeeds under a junior disciple, and death sends characters through the underworld (阴阳界), where Judge Cui reviews the register of life and death and revives them with a real stat penalty.

libs.name: 夕阳三-炎龙美化版
libs.english_name: Sunset Reappears III: Seal of the Fire Dragon (Fire Dragon Edition)
libs.english_description: Branded "Sunset Reappears III: Seal of the Fire Dragon" by AKAI Studio, but its actual world map isn't Sunset Reappears content at all -- file comparison confirms it shares the unrelated "Tianya" (Edge of Heaven) family's map data byte-for-byte with six other archives in this collection (tybxjh, wlhd, xhcii, zxty, ffxymud, jhfy2), making this the seventh confirmed Tianya-lineage member found so far; the genuine Sunset Reappears map lives instead in this collection's unrelated xajh4gkb/jhfy3/xyzx siblings. It also shares the old Tomud/"Smiling Proud Wanderer" client handshake with the xyj2006 family (the first line after connecting must be the literal "2060"). A near-identical twin, xyzx3 (also titled Sunset Reappears III: Seal of the Fire Dragon), appears to be the same original archive split into two separate entries in this project (matching file count, directory layout, and map data). New characters start in the Quanzhou region, at a temple called Iron Spear Temple, and can later join the Beggars' Sect at its Chengdu branch hall, working up through named disciple ranks.

libs.name: 小雨西游utf8
libs.english_name: Light Rain Journey to the West (UTF-8 Snapshot)
libs.english_description: Another independent archive of the Xiaoyu Xiyou / Xiaoyu Xiyou II engine, its filename flagging that it had already been pre-converted to UTF-8. Though it shares an engine family with this project's xyxy2 and xiaoyuxiyou snapshots -- including the same Aolai Kingdom newbie zone (safe sparring, an NPC-taught two-step skill-learning flow, a starting-inn shop and message board) -- a content-hash comparison shows it is not a byte-for-byte duplicate of either (8,753 vs. 11,149 .lpc files); it's a snapshot from a different point in the game's development, not just a re-encoding, so it was processed as its own distinct archive. Beyond the shared newbie content, this build layers a level-gated spell/dungeon progression under daemon/class/spells/40/, numbered in tiers players "break through" as they level.

libs.name: 夕阳再现
libs.english_name: Sunset Reappears: Storm Rises Again II
libs.english_description: The "Storm Rises Again II" branch of the true Sunset Reappears lineage: unlike its similarly-"Sunset Reappears"-branded siblings xysylmhb and xyzxiiylzymh (whose maps actually belong to the unrelated "Tianya" family), this archive's world data really is byte-identical to jhfy3, xajh4gkb, and xyzxyl201412 -- four snapshots of the same authored map running on different security-layer implementations. New characters start not at the genre's usual South City Inn but at Northern Frontier Town, an unusually rare Central-Asian-flavored setting for this corpus, with an adjoining Bai's Family Courtyard (named for a term for a wealthy landowner in Xinjiang) evoking a frontier backdrop rather than the standard Jiangnan wuxia one. Its login/registration flow closely mirrors xysylmhb's (the same dual admin-password/login-password scheme), but unlike xysylmhb, this build's standard port skips the old Tomud client handshake entirely -- the literal "2060" version check only fires on a separate, dedicated Tomud-only port.

libs.archive: 夕阳再现II-炎龙专用美化客户端.rar
libs.name: 夕阳再现II-炎龙专用美化客户端
libs.english_name: Sunset Reappears II: Fire Dragon Client Edition
libs.english_description: Another build of Sunset Reappears III: Seal of the Fire Dragon by AKAI Studio, in the same family as xysylmhb (Sunset III: Fire Dragon Edition), and likewise using the old Tomud client handshake protocol. As with xysylmhb, its map actually belongs to the unrelated "Tianya" family rather than the true Sunset Reappears lineage — another case in this collection where the title's branding doesn't match the underlying code's true origin.

libs.name: 夕阳再现-炎龙20141231
libs.english_name: Sunset Reappears: Fire Dragon Edition (2014-12-31 Build)
libs.english_description: The most expanded surviving build in the genuine Sunset Reappears map lineage (shared with this project's xyzxfk, xyzxfy2, xyzx, jhfy3, and xajh4gkb): the same core jianghu map has been extended with overseas regions in Japan (d/japan/) and Korea (d/gaoli/) plus an auto-mapping feature (d/automap/) not present in its siblings. A file-level comparison confirms it shares ~93-94% of its common-path world files byte-for-byte with both xyzxfk and xyzxfy2, so this is the same authored map carried forward rather than a rewrite. It also layers on its own distinctive character-creation step (choosing one of eleven schools of magic after stat allocation), a custom wizard rank ladder running all the way up to "(boss)"/"(ceo)", and support for multiple client protocols (ZMud/ToMud).

libs.name: 炎黄武魂public-final-2016-12-08
libs.english_name: Tales of Wulin Heroes: Soul of Yan-Huang (Public Final, 2016-12-08 Build)
libs.english_description: In-game the title reads "Tales of Wulin Heroes: Soul of Yan-Huang" — the master.lpc header traces the full ancestry: ES II → Annihilator → Xiang's XKX → Doing Lu's hell (2K) → Linux@lxtx's 2003 "yh" branch. A file-level comparison found this archive is a near-duplicate of this collection's yanhuangwuhun (96% of common files byte-identical, same 73-zone map) — that sibling even appends a "II" to its own in-game title to tell the two apart. It's also closely related (87-89% overlap) to sibling yhyxs, a third, differently-branded snapshot of the same lxtx-2003 codebase ("Chronicle of Yan-Huang Heroes"). All three inherit hell's underworld reincarnation ritual (Yama's Hall, the Pool of Forgetfulness), though this build simplifies chargen to a direct five-way archetype pick (Warrior/Sage/Endurance/Agility/Balanced) with split surname/given-name entry, dual admin/login passwords, and no email step.

libs.name: 浴血江湖
libs.english_name: Blood-Soaked Jianghu III: Return to the Jianghu
libs.english_description: Blood-Soaked Jianghu III: Return to the Jianghu, published by KMMUD.COM. New characters start at the Iron Spear Temple, a rural shrine honoring the Five Dynasties general Wang Yanzhang, with a crow-nested watchtower beside it; the combat system resolves attack, dodge, defense, and parry as separate numbers, with move descriptions varying by body part and weapon. Registration runs through an English ID, a full Chinese name entered as a single string (no separate surname/given-name split), a dual-password system (admin password plus login password), a talent menu (0 for a random full set, y to accept), email, and gender. It belongs to this collection's 'Tianya' family — its signature cliff-jump scene is byte-for-byte identical to sibling wlhd's (Wulin Haodang / Jin Yong's Dream II) independently rewritten version, a lineage relationship no earlier archive here had documented — and shares roughly 85% of its file paths with fellow Tianya member yzxiiizylfy (Sunset Reborn III), though only about a third of that shared scaffold is byte-identical content, making the two diverged siblings rather than a duplicate pair.

libs.name: 逸侠世界
libs.english_description: Daniel's World (逸俠之世界), part of the ES II engine family, produced in Taiwan (BBS 140.127.179.161; contact leonguo@tpts4.seed.net.tw). Unusually for this corpus, new characters start on a modern campus (classrooms, a courtyard garden, a lab building, a kitchen, a bike rack) rather than the usual wuxia inn or martial hall, and the world folds in scenes and NPCs from Taiwan's Pili Puppetry (霹靂布袋戲) glove-puppet franchise alongside the standard jianghu backdrop. Registration runs through an English ID, Chinese name, password with confirmation, email, and gender. Shares the same codebase, title, and contact email with this collection's yxzsj, an independent build from a different point in the same game's history (not a byte-identical repackaging).

libs.name: 游侠笑传II
libs.english_name: The Wandering Knight's Comic Saga II
libs.english_description: The Wandering Knight's Comic Saga II, live since October 1999. Its sect map is a Jin Yong multi-novel crossover spanning Shaolin, Huashan, Emei, Songshan, and Taishan (The Smiling, Proud Wanderer's Five Mountain Schools) alongside Mingjiao and the Sun Moon Holy Cult's Black Wood Cliff from the same novel, the Ancient Tomb sect and Quanzhen Sect from Return of the Condor Heroes, Peach Blossom Island from Legend of the Condor Heroes, the Vulture Palace from Demi-Gods and Semi-Devils, and the Divine Dragon Cult from The Deer and the Cauldron. Admin rank uses its own Chinese title scheme ('主管巫师', not the usual bracketed '(admin)'). Supports dual-encoding clients — after connecting, players choose GB or BIG5 encoding, and the BIG5 prompt line deliberately appears garbled when viewed under GBK, an intentional design touch rather than an encoding bug. Registration runs through encoding choice, English ID, Chinese name, password with confirmation, talent selection (y to accept), email, and gender.

libs.archive: 逸  俠  之  世  界.rar
libs.name: 逸  俠  之  世  界
libs.english_description: Daniel's World, the same ES II-family, Taiwan-produced game as this collection's yxsj — including its unusual modern-campus starting map (classrooms, courtyard garden, lab building, kitchen, bike rack) and the Taiwanese Pili Puppetry (霹靂布袋戲) glove-puppet scenes woven into the jianghu backdrop — but a distinct build from a different point in the codebase's history: same title, same contact email, and the same file structure, yet not a byte-identical repackaging (its combatd.lpc, for instance, differs from yxsj's by roughly 80 lines) — worth keeping as a separate entry rather than treating as a duplicate.

libs.name: 阳再线III之炎龙封印
libs.english_name: Sunset Reborn III: Seal of the Flame Dragon
libs.english_description: Sunset Reborn III: Seal of the Flame Dragon, produced by AKAI Studio in 2006. Like the other 'Sunset Reborn'-titled archives in this collection, it uses the Tomud '2060' client handshake, rejecting any first input that isn't literally the string '2060' before asking for an English ID. Despite the 'Sunset Reborn' title, its map actually belongs to the unrelated 'Tianya' lineage (its signature cliff-jump scene is byte-for-byte identical to xysylmhb/xyzxiiylzymh) rather than the true 'Sunset Reborn' family (xyzx/jhfy3/xajh4gkb/xyzxyl201412) — the tenth confirmed 'Tianya' family member found in this collection. New characters land at the same Iron Spear Temple starting shrine as this collection's yxjh, and a file-level comparison confirms the kinship is real but partial: roughly 85% of yxjh's file paths exist here too (the same Tianya scaffold, including matching heimuya/quanzhou/gaibang zone directories), but only about a third of that shared scaffold is byte-identical content — a diverged sibling rather than a repackaged duplicate.

libs.name: 终极地狱2008完整版
libs.english_description: Ultimate Hell 2008: Complete Edition ('Revive of Ultra Hell (Blood & Magic)', originally from 1999.11.13, produced by CDS). Part of this collection's wider 'Doing'/Hell-lineage family rooted in the hell archive — its master.lpc, logind.lpc, named.lpc, and versiond.lpc are structured almost line-for-line the same. A byte-level, line-ending-normalized comparison of the /d room tree confirms the shared world runs deeper than the engine files: this build is 88% identical to hell's own map, and even closer to its own zjdy-branded siblings — 95% to zjdyaryl, 90% to zjdyzj, and 76% to both zjdywzb and zjmudhell — so all six archives (hell, zjdy2008wzb, zjdyaryl, zjdywzb, zjdyzj, zjmudhell) are snapshots/variants of one authored wuxia world rather than independently-designed games. This edition's own distinguishing touches: registration splits surname and given name into separate prompts and adds an explicit 1-5 character-type menu, new characters start from 'Peach Blossom Spring' (世外桃源) rather than the more common south-city inn, and the sect map includes 'Dragon Slaying' (屠龙) and 'Blood Blade' (血刀) rooms nodding to specific Jin Yong weapons/factions alongside the standard Shaolin/Wudang/Emei/Beggars'-Sect/Mingjiao roster.

libs.name: 终极地狱完整版
libs.english_description: Ultimate Hell: Complete Edition (in-game banner: 'Emperor of Ultra Hell (Blood & Magic), from 2002.06.2'). Part of the same six-way 'Hell'/Doing-lineage map family as this collection's hell, zjdy2008wzb, zjdyaryl, zjdyzj, and zjmudhell (the original archive was itself named hell) — its adm/single/master.lpc, logind.lpc and named.lpc are structurally near-identical to zjdy2008wzb's, and a byte-level, line-ending-normalized room-tree comparison found the shared map is roughly 67-76% identical across the family (closest to zjdy2008wzb, more diverged from the tighter zjdyaryl/zjdyzj cluster), covering the same Shaolin/Wudang/Emei/Beggars'-Sect/'Dragon Slaying'/'Blood Blade' zones. This build's own versiond.lpc (2,194 lines) is a substantially more complete build/sync daemon than zjdy2008wzb's. It includes 43 bulletin boards spread across its sect and city zones.

libs.name: 再现天涯
libs.english_description: Tianya Reborn (in-game banner: 'Dream Return to Tianya'). Unrelated to the Doing-lineage 'Hell' family covered elsewhere in this collection, but shares the same source code as this collection's wider 'Tianya' family — its 'Peak of the World' cliff-jump scene is byte-for-byte identical to tybxjh (the lineage's root), xhcii, ffxymud, jhfy2, xysylmhb, and xyzxiiylzymh, while wlhd shares the same map but independently rewrote that one room. Its wizard hierarchy tops out one rank differently from most siblings, at (boss) rather than (admin). Character creation takes a single combined 2-4 character name (unlike the separate surname/given-name split used by the zjdywzb-family titles) with a random attribute-talent menu, starting new characters at the Inn of Leisure. A 2008 revised re-release of this same game is also in this collection as zxty08nxgbb. Its bulletin-board system spans 105 boards across the sect and city zones.

libs.name: 再现天涯（08年修改版本）
libs.english_description: The 2008 revised re-release of the same 'Tianya Reborn' game as this collection's zxty (and, through it, the wider 'Tianya' family sharing the byte-identical 'Peak of the World' cliff-jump scene) — the master.lpc content differs with no exact hash match, but the map is essentially unchanged and it shares the same title and origin. Its own registration-room implementation (named.lpc) turns out to share its exact design with this collection's unrelated NT/nitan family (e.g. nt1), rather than only with sibling zxty/jym as previously assumed — a cross-family infrastructure link not otherwise documented. Its quit command has a genuine anti-abuse mechanism: a new account logged in for under 30 minutes must press quit twice to actually exit without saving, a deliberate design choice rather than a bug.

libs.name: 郑州风云3
libs.english_description: Zhengzhou Storm 3 (in-game banner: 'Fengyun Series: Invincible Under Heaven'), a Gu Long-style wuxia MUD founded by Xgchen ('Elder Sun Wuqing'). Shares the same 'Zhengzhou Storm' map and codebase as this collection's wqfy ('Heartless Storm', which carries the same 'Invincible Under Heaven' banner) — a relationship neither archive's documentation had previously noted. It also turns out to be a near-duplicate of this collection's other 'Zhengzhou Storm 3' archive (zzfy): same engine and map, over 10,000 files nearly all identical, differing in fewer than 200 — the two are kept as separate entries rather than merged.

libs.name: 武学大道
libs.english_name: Wu Xue Da Dao (The Great Way of Martial Arts)
libs.english_description: A wuxia MUD that begins in the "Peach Blossom Spring," a legendary hidden utopia, built around a non-standard mobile-client protocol rather than plain-text telnet prompts. New characters must complete an elaborate, multi-step "rebirth" ritual — allocating attribute points, rerolling aptitudes, choosing a temperament, and picking one of seven ancestral clans — before they truly enter the world.

libs.name: 泥潭6
libs.english_description: A large NT/nitan ('Mire') lineage wuxia mudlib built on a creation myth — Pangu splitting heaven and earth, yin and yang emerging from chaos — and spanning over 23,000 source files, making it one of the largest games in this collection. Its signature touch is a 'birth ceremony': after registering, `score` reports the character as not yet 'born' until they travel to the Registration realm and complete a ritual dialogue with mythic NPCs Pangu and Ksitigarbha (地藏王/Earth Treasury Bodhisattva), weaving the tutorial gate directly into the game's own mythology rather than just an email-confirmation step. The map stretches from the Central Chinese heartland cities of Chang'an and Luoyang out to Annam (Vietnam), Korea, Kazakhstan, and Taiwan. A separate database-free 'win_nodb' packaging of this same world also exists in this collection as nt6nitan6win, sharing the same registration-room mechanic plus its own dedicated 'reborn' area.

libs.name: 泥潭6 (win_nodb版)
libs.english_description: A same-lineage variant of nt6 (Mire 6), packaged as a database-free 'win_nodb' build sharing the same underlying codebase file-for-file. It shares nt6's sprawling map, stretching from the central Chinese heartland cities of Chang'an and Luoyang out to Annam (Vietnam), Korea, Kazakhstan, and Taiwan, plus its own dedicated 'reborn' area layered onto the same registration-room mechanic.

libs.name: 妖神之争
libs.english_description: A xianxia MUD set in the mythological world of Journey to the West, with new characters entering through the pilgrimage-to-the-West framework and starting at the South City Inn in Chang'an. Its eight-stat talent system (Strength/Courage/Comprehension/Spirituality/Composure/Looks/Constitution/Fortune) feeds a two-camp, ten-sect roster split along the novel's own good-versus-evil axis: five "Divine" sects (Five Villages Temple, Moon Palace, Dragon Palace, Putuo, Fangcun Mountain) against five "Demon" sects (Bottomless Cave, Xuanyuan's Ancient Tomb, Water Curtain Cave, Great Snow Mountain, the Underworld), each favoring different builds of fist/weapon/spell/internal-power/lightness-skill and gated on gender and Looks — the newbie manual even notes some demon sects specifically want a LOW Looks score. Death is a full afterlife ritual: Judge Cui Jue of the Vermilion Brush escorts the ghost to the Yin-Yang Boundary, with automatic revival after a short wait.

libs.archive: 南京河海大学的es2和xkx《校内_1.01版》.tar.gz
libs.name: es2/侠客行（南京河海大学校内版1.01）
libs.english_name: Eastern Story II x Xiake Xing (Hohai University Campus Edition)
libs.english_description: A hybrid of the ES2 and Xiake Xing ('The Wandering Knight') engine lineages, built as a computer-science-department test build at Hohai University in Nanjing, with a standard shared wuxia sect map (Shaolin, Wudang, Huashan, Taishan, Mingjiao, Beggars'-Sect, Peach-Blossom Island). The content is still a work in progress, but the world already has personality — the pawnshop owner in Snow Pavilion Town (安惜迩) is secretly a hidden master with far more combat prowess than any other early-game NPC, useful as a deliberately unbeatable trigger for testing the death-and-revival flow, while the doorkeeper at the Chunfeng martial arts hall (刘安禄) hides a real secret identity behind his everyday flavor text: ask him the right question — naming 'Bloody-Hand Liu San' — while you're experienced enough yourself, and he drops the disguise, reveals himself as the deputy chief of Wild-Goat-Mountain's bandits, and comes at you at more than double his original strength.

libs.name: 海洋（基础版）
libs.english_description: A wuxia MUD set in the world of Jin Yong's novels (new characters are asked not to reuse the novels' own character names), whose community calls itself the Qingyimeng, the "Covenant of Passion and Righteousness." Despite sharing the "Ocean" name with this project's hy2000/hy2002/hy5, a comparison found no lineage relationship -- master file hashes and securd.lpc/feature/skill.lpc don't match any of them. Characters roll four attributes -- strength, comprehension, physique, and agility -- and can randomize any or all of them at creation. New characters progress from registration through the newbie sequence (inn, West Main Street, Yangzhou martial hall), a Central Square brawl, death, the five-part Ghost-Gate dialogue with the White-Robed Ghost, and revival at the martial temple; the bulletin board's post/look chain also works end to end. Night genuinely darkens the map -- bare direction words like "north" stop working after dark with a "too dark to see" message, forcing "go <direction>" instead -- an intentional day/night mechanic, not a bug.

libs.name: 海洋5
libs.english_description: The community calls this world "Ocean V," and despite the "hy" slug prefix suggesting kinship with hy/hy2000/hy2002 (this project's other "Ocean"-titled family), a file comparison shows hy5 is actually much closer to a different sibling: haiyang2 (Ocean II / Star-Moon Legend) elsewhere in this collection. Its adm/obj/master.lpc is byte-for-byte identical to haiyang2's, and a large sample of domain files came back roughly 90% byte-identical too — the two are effectively the same base world, not just "another branch of the Ocean line." hy5's own security daemon (securd.lpc) has been independently rewritten, and it extends haiyang2's ~141-zone map with roughly 50 more regions — Annan (Vietnam), Gaoli (Korea), a Japan region (Kobe/Kyoto), Tibet, Xinjiang, Loulan, Taiwan — making its total map one of the largest in this project, though the extension (not the whole map) is what's genuinely distinct here. It also carries the family's marriage system, a GB/Big5 character-set prompt that reads like a yes/no question but only accepts gb/g or big5/b (answering y/n loops forever), and an unusually layered new-character death-protection stack (a combat-experience threshold, safe zones, and a separate near-death auto-full-heal-once effect) that makes a natural death rare for new characters.

libs.name: 金庸梦
libs.english_description: A wuxia MUD that deliberately blends the sect systems of several different Jin Yong novels into one shared world: newcomers arrive at a Hall of Heroes where Jin Yong himself appears as a friendly, talkative NPC who introduces all 12 joinable sects — the Beggars' Sect, Quanzhen Sect, and Peach Blossom Island from Condor Heroes; the Tianlong Babu-era Ming Cult, Xingxiu Sect, and White Camel Manor; the Sunflower Manual world's Mount Hua and Shaolin; and more, crossing Legend of the Condor Heroes, Demi-Gods and Semi-Devils, Swordsman, and Heaven Sword and Dragon Saber into a single continuity. Registration uniquely splits the account password from a separate 10+ character "recovery password." Its map directory structure heavily overlaps with this project's xkx2000zxb (Ode to Gallantry 2000, Latest Edition, MudOS v22b25 lineage) — scenes such as the ancestral hall at the Lake Tai ancient tomb are identical, differing only in the "cracked by" credit in the file headers ("Cracked by Kafei" there versus "Cracked by Roath" here) — indicating both are different circulating copies of the same underlying "Ode to Gallantry I" codebase, a relationship neither archive had previously recorded. xkm (Ode to Gallantry's Dream) and bmxkx2001 (Ode to Gallantry, North America 2001 Edition) are sibling archives from the same "Cracked by Roath" release line.

libs.name: 泥潭1
libs.english_description: An independent branch of the NT/nitan ('Mire') engine family, with no exact code match to sibling games nitan170911, nitan6, or hhsj — it grew up on its own. New characters must first pass through a 'registration room' and use a built-in register-with-email command before their attributes are even assigned, an extra gate reminiscent of the 'reincarnation' step found in the Hell/Doing family of games. Character creation also layers a temperament type and a character-class type on top of the usual gender choice.

libs.name: 武动仙途
libs.english_name: Wu Dong Xian Tu (Martial Path to Immortality)
libs.english_description: A large, 46,890-file archive built for a dedicated GUI client rather than plain telnet: on connecting, the server issues a version challenge the client must answer with a correctly encrypted response (or one of two built-in bypass strings) or be disconnected as an "illegal client," and registration/character-creation fields arrive as single lines separated by a full-width vertical bar (║) rather than one prompt at a time — neither is a bug. Alongside a standard Jin Yong sect map (Huashan, Wudang, Emei, the Beggars' Sect, Ming Cult), it layers on a full modern MMORPG-style instanced-dungeon system (副本/"fuben" zones, including named boss instances) that is unusually elaborate for this generation of mudlib, plus a real payment-callback service (payd.lpc) — evidence this install was once wired up to an actual web-recharge storefront rather than being a purely free text MUD. Shares its connection protocol and mixin architecture with this collection's NT/nitan/Lonely-lineage libs (xfbhh, hhsj, nt1, nitan170911), with its own additional F_SUIT mixin.

libs.name: 侠客梦
libs.english_description: A wuxia MUD from the same "Ode to Gallantry I" codebase lineage as this project's jym (Jin Yong's Dream) and xkx2000zxb -- all three are separately circulating copies of one underlying archive, sharing the same simul_efuns and the same roughly 50-zone map skeleton (Taihu Ancient Tomb, Kunlun, Shaolin, Wudang, Emei, the Beggars' Sect, the Sun-Moon Holy Cult, Peach Blossom Island, and more), though xkm's own registration flow adds two steps unique to this copy -- confirming you've read the "Xiake Meng player code of conduct" and supplying a QQ number -- so its connection sequence should not be assumed identical to jym's. New characters wash up on the beach at Xiakedao ("Isle of the Chivalrous"), greeted by a smiling fisherman, before heading out to join sects and build a reputation. Its standout mechanic is a custom equipment-forging system: high-level players who gather rare materials (a sea-bottom "Golden Mother" relic, thousand-year spirit wood) can commission the legendary smith Mo Ye to forge a weapon or suit of armor at the Mysterious-Weapon Ancient Cave, temper it through training, and pay the Taoist master Zhang Tianshi at a Western-Regions immortal's cave to socket it with gems earned by killing assassins or exploring a maze. Dying more than 200 times without reaching 50,000 combat experience permanently locks a character in a death-penalty room.

libs.name: 风起云涌2
libs.english_description: Part of the same "Ocean" codebase lineage as several sibling archives in this project, sharing their distinctive hardcoded backdoor admin mechanism. Features a larger-than-usual map including the classic sects alongside an independent Assassins' Tower faction and a marriage system, blending social and underworld gameplay. Its admin roster is stored not in a plain text file but inside the security daemon's own save data.

libs.name: 风云II（美国版本）
libs.english_description: A wuxia MUD set in Gu Long's jianghu, built on the "Jinyong Qunxiazhuan"/XKX framework — it shares the same adm/obj/master.lpc as siblings jyqxc, jyqxc2, jyqxc2013fwq, and xkx2017. It was previously catalogued as having "entirely different" game content from every other sibling, but a file-level check found that overstated: roughly 30% of its domain files are byte-identical to fy330's (also an XKX-framework game), including the exact room-name skeleton for the central Fengqiuhuang square and Chenxiang Town — both draw on the same underlying Fengyun-world template, each independently re-skinned on top of it rather than built from nothing. Distinctive touches of its own: a registration password rule requiring mixed case plus a special character (matched byte-for-byte by fy330, but stricter than most of this collection), ethnicity selection at signup, wounds that permanently lower a character's HP ceiling instead of just draining current HP, and government constables who — unlike most NPCs in this collection — actively chase fleeing players into adjacent rooms.

libs.name: 风云III (3.0)
libs.english_description: Storm III v3.0. Despite a master-file mismatch that put it under its own number, a file-level check found its actual game world is not a standalone creation: its domain tree is 90-96% byte-identical to siblings fy3dz (Storm III Collector's Edition) and fy3xd (Xingxing's Revision), sharing the same map for Shaolin, Huangshan, Songshan, Taishan, and a dozen other named areas almost file-for-file — these three are successive snapshots of one "Storm III" world rather than independently written games (fy330 looks like the plainest/earliest cut; fy3dz layers in a couple of extra zones on top). It also shares login/registration framework code (check_legal_name, password rules, ethnicity selection, all byte-for-byte) with fy2mg, and — less expected given the two are usually described as unrelated — roughly 30% of its actual domain files literally match fy2mg's too, including the central Fengqiuhuang square's room-name skeleton; the wider "Fengyun"/Storm lineage across this collection clearly grew from one shared base template. On its own terms: a Gu Long-style jianghu starting at the chatty, heartbeat-driven Fengqiuhuang Inn, with a fully fleshed-out Shaolin apprenticeship ladder (15th-to-23rd-generation disciples up through an abbot who demands a hidden trial be passed first) and a combat auto-flee safety net.

libs.name: 雄霸天下III
libs.english_name: Xiong Ba Tian Xia III (Lord of the World III)
libs.english_description: A genuine 1997-2001-era mudlib, by its own author's admission a deliberate patchwork rather than a single lineage: the archive's own bundled readme tells players not to bother exploring most of the map because it stitches together zones borrowed from the ES2, XKX, and Fengyun codebases, plus one original area — a foggy island inspired by the novel "Wizard's Diary," begun as an East-meets-West collaboration that was abandoned when the group lost its server. (A separate, unrelated archive in this collection, ldtx, uses the same in-game "Xiongba Tianxia" brand name but was confirmed to share only a distant common ES II ancestor, not this codebase.) The author's own notes single out its combat system as the standout feature: fights play out on tactical 3x3/5x5/7x7 grids with real positioning and distance-based spell ranges, a more tactical layout than the typical single-room exchange. Character creation otherwise blends Western MUD-style classes (a choice between enchanter and fighter) with the wuxia setting, and death leads into an unusually elaborate five-stage ghost journey — Ghost Gate Road, the Naihe Bridge, the gates of Fengdu, the Hall of Sen Luo, and Hell's entrance — narrated throughout by the deity Bai Wuchang and adjudicated by King Yama himself. The original archive shipped as four split zip volumes containing twelve directory-by-directory tar.gz files rather than a flat directory tree.

libs.archive: 侠客行老版(金庸群侠传）.rar
libs.name: 侠客行（老版/金庸群侠传）
libs.english_name: Ode to Gallantry (Old Edition / Heroes of Jin Yong)
libs.english_description: A wuxia MUD whose map is a genuine Jin Yong multi-novel mashup rather than a single-book setting: alongside the standard Huashan/Wudang/Shaolin/Beggars' Sect roster shared with the jyqxc/jyqxc2 family, it includes Tianlongsi (the Tianlong Monastery from Demi-Gods and Semi-Devils), Heimuya (Black Wood Cliff, home of the Sun Moon Holy Cult from The Smiling, Proud Wanderer), Taohua/Peach Blossom Island (Legend of the Condor Heroes), and a Mystic Dragon Cult hall (The Deer and the Cauldron). One archival curiosity: extracted from a mislabeled ".rar" that is actually a POSIX tar file, it also carries an unused adm/obj/master.lpc byte-identical to the jyqxc/fy2mg/xkx2017 framework master, but the game actually boots from a different file, /adm/single/master, so this look-alike was never really loaded — a red herring for lineage-tracing rather than a real shared codebase link.

libs.name: 西游记 4.2
libs.english_description: An independent Journey to the West mythology implementation with a fuller mythological map than most siblings in this family -- the Thirty-Three Heavens, the Garden of Immortal Peaches, Penglai, and the Heavenly Palace are all built out, plus a guild-hall zone (d/banghui/) unique to this archive. New characters can apprentice into the Lingtai Fangcun Mountain sect under disciple Yun Qing, and a poem-guessing minigame quizzes players with real Tang-dynasty poetry drawn from a library of hundreds of poems (confirmed real works by Pei Di and Gao Shi, not placeholder text). Death sends characters to the underworld (阴阳界), where Judge Cui reviews the register of life and death and resurrects them at a waystation.

libs.name: 西游记4.2 (dup)
libs.group_note: line-ending-only duplicate of 156 (xyj42, archive 西游记4.2.gz) -- identical file tree, every file differs only by CRLF vs LF; processed once

libs.archive: 最新独立安卓客户端和书剑源码一键架站.zip
libs.name: 书剑3
libs.english_description: Extracted from a nested archive that also bundled an Android client APK alongside this source tree, which uses it: connecting players get a one-shot handshake banner and then submit account/password/nickname/gender fields via a custom delimiter-based mobile protocol rather than the usual line-by-line prompts. Despite the shared "Book and Sword" branding, it shares no code lineage with bxsj/bxsj1 or any other library in this collection — an entirely independent codebase, richer than a simple sect-and-map layout thanks to instanced dungeon content (`d/fuben/`) plus dedicated music and guild areas, with apprenticeship into the Wudang sect, sect-map travel, combat, death, and a Ghost Gate revival cycle among its systems.

libs.name: 指尖MUD
libs.english_description: Extracted from a nested archive (zjmud.7z, containing a folder named 'hell'). Its core system files (master.lpc, logind.lpc, and others) were heavily rewritten to support a custom mobile-phone client protocol — different master-file hash, different registration flow — but the map itself belongs to the same six-way 'Hell'/Doing-lineage family as this collection's hell, zjdy2008wzb, zjdyaryl, zjdywzb, and zjdyzj: a byte-level, line-ending-normalized comparison found its /d room tree 83% identical to zjdyzj, 79% to zjdyaryl, 76% to zjdy2008wzb, and 67% to both hell and zjdywzb — the entire sect-and-city world ported onto an independently developed mobile client engine rather than a simple in-engine derivative. It shares the same mobile-app protocol and custom logind.lpc lineage as shujian3, and unlike shujian3 its password field is genuinely cryptographically verified (a real crypt(ZJKEY, ...) challenge with no bypass string) — the most carefully-implemented of this family's mobile protocols. The system rewrite came at a cost: legacy features tied to the old core (bulletin-board posting, player-run shops, mail) were never carried over to the new engine and simply don't exist here.

libs.name: DeadSouls-FluffOS2019
libs.english_description: The fluffos GitHub org's own actively-maintained fork of the classic Dead Souls 3.8.6 mudlib, pre-adapted for the modern FluffOS v2019 driver branch (tracked as a git submodule) rather than a legacy archive dump -- a separate, independently-sourced snapshot from this collection's other two Dead Souls entries (ds386, dshakkard), already carrying its own AUTO_WIZ registration, a websocket listener, and a www/ web client. New characters begin in "The start room" near the Praxis campus, then `enter town` to reach the main city; playable races are dwarf, elf, half-elf, half-orc, halfling, human, orc, and poleepkwa. The town/campus/Praxis/amigara/learning/Ylsrim/cave/examples domains are Dead Souls' own official "how to build an area" teaching material, and AUTO_WIZ lets a new registrant answer "creator" instead of "player" to get builder access immediately, with `read chapter 1 in handbook` as the suggested first step.

libs.archive: git clone https://github.com/fluffos/nightmare3 (not a traditional archive file — a maintained, already FluffOS-adapted fork; mudlib root is the repo's lib/ directory)
libs.name: Nightmare 3
libs.english_description: One of the oldest and most historically influential LPMud mudlib families, an ancestor of the TMI-2 lineage. This fork (fluffos/nightmare3) is already updated for modern FluffOS. New characters pick a race in a genesis void room before rolling stats and entering Praxis, the mudlib's own shipped example domain — a full town with shops, a bank, a graveyard, mountain caves, and an orc valley — built around a central Monument Square, with five playable classes (fighter, cleric, mage, rogue, kataan) and three joinable guilds (druids, philosophers, witches). Unlike the rest of this collection, content is in English, included deliberately for its historical importance to the wider LPMud family tree.

libs.name: IMUD@FluffOS.v2019
libs.english_description: The FluffOS project's own tiny live demo at imud.fluffos.info, not a game: connecting drops you straight into an anonymous session (no login, no registration, no player object/save data, no rooms) with exactly two commands, mudlist (lists the real, live Intermud-3 network via a genuine outbound socket connection to the *i4 router) and update (reload an object by path). Included as a preserved reference example of a minimal from-scratch FluffOS mudlib/I3-client rather than a wuxia game.

libs.name: 三国志
libs.english_description: A Three-Kingdoms-themed Chinese MUD built on the Lima mudlib base (TMI-2/Ellery security lineage). Players start from a Lima-style wizard hall, roll a talent template (valor/strategy/charisma archetypes), and build a career across a real map of Three-Kingdoms-era cities, garrisons and nations -- recruiting personal troops, riding named historical horses, and taking government office.

libs.archive: git clone https://github.com/fluffos/nt7 (王者归来, "泥潭7" — already a UTF-8/FluffOS-v2019-adapted community fork, not a raw legacy archive)
libs.name: 王者归来
libs.english_description: A member of the NT/nitan/Lonely engine family (see nitan170911, nitan6, hhsj, xfbhh, nt1, nt6). Core daemons (master.lpc, logind.lpc, securityd.lpc, chinesed.lpc) share the family's overall shape but have diverged substantially in content from every sibling checked (hundreds to thousands of differing lines even after whitespace normalization) -- a real independent branch, not a duplicate. New characters undergo the same Pangu creation-myth 'birth ceremony' as hhsj/nt6 (choose a personality, wash attributes in the Valley of Life, land in the Ancient Village).

libs.name: Lima
libs.english_description: The FluffOS driver project's own official reference mudlib (limalib.dev) -- an English-language, developer-facing framework built to demonstrate what a modern LPC mudlib looks like, quite unlike the classic Chinese wuxia lineages that make up most of this collection. Rather than registering one verb per add_action, Lima understands full natural-language sentences ('take the red potion from the box'), secures files and commands through a capability-based system of privileges/domains/protections instead of the traditional uid/root model, and gives every wizard a Unix-like shell (variables, pipes, globbing) rather than a fixed command table. New characters begin in the Grand Hall, a wizards' meeting room with polished floorboards and rough-hewn beams, flanked by a sulfurous northwest passage, a passage to the south that smells like something recently died, and an incongruous elevator door to the west; a glowing portal leads to the separate mortal starting area. Bundled demo content includes a nine-room 'Sandy Beach' pirate treasure-hunting puzzle (explicitly marked by its own author as not meant for a real, live mud) and optional contributed modules for bulletin boards, marriage, and in-room object creation. New characters are granted wizard powers automatically (AUTO_WIZ), the upstream project's own default for a framework meant to be explored and extended, not played as a finished game.

libs.name: 东方故事Ⅱ
libs.english_description: One of the earliest Chinese-language LPC mudlibs -- GitHub's mudchina org describes it as "the progenitor of Chinese MUDs" (中文MUD鼻祖). A from-scratch LPMud-lineage codebase (credited to Annihilator@Eastern.Stories, 1994-1995, built on the Lil mudlib with TMI feature-mixin code) rather than a reskin of an existing engine -- this project's own recurring "ES2/TMI-2/Falcon family" terminology for dozens of later Chinese mudlibs traces back to this exact lineage. Players register with a real Chinese name, land at a mountain inn (饮风客栈), and explore a wuxia/xianxia world of domains (city gates and streets, snow-capped mountains, a temple, a bamboo canyon, a ghost/graveyard area) with guild-style skill training, a two-tier reputation system, and NPCs including a Dragon Ball crossover cameo (孙悟空/Son Goku, described in-game as ESII's first self-growing NPC whose combat experience permanently accumulates from the moment he's created).

libs.name: Genesis
libs.english_description: The official mudlib of Genesis, one of the oldest and most influential LPMuds still running. This is the engine only (master, login, std/ base classes, command souls, board/mail/bank/donation/report subsystems, the full wizard toolset) -- per the repo's own README, it ships no /d/Genesis game-world domain at all (no rooms, no NPCs, no items, no race content). Since no domain ships to place new characters in, this collection's copy adds a from-scratch character-creation bootstrap and a bare landing room so the engine is actually playable.

libs.name: RealmsMUD core-lib
libs.english_description: The official mudlib of RealmsMUD, a modern, actively-developed engine with a substantial shipped game world rather than a bare framework. New characters pass through an 11-step creation wizard (terminal color/charset setup, a live minimap demo, gender, race and subrace, hair and eye color, attribute allocation, and skill/trait selection) before landing in the world proper. 27 guilds span elemental casters (Aeromancer, Aquamancer, Cryomancer, Geomancer, Pyromancer), classic archetypes (Fighter, Mage, Ranger, Rogue, Bard, Druid, Necromancer), and setting-specific orders with their own lore (the Aegis Guard, the League of Assassins, the Hand of Bilanx, the Guardian of Khazurath, the Children of Ilyrth, Disciples of Argloth and Ferianth, the Werric Knights, Wrathguard, Runeskald, Oneiromancer, and Therianthrope shapeshifters). The shipped world includes named regions Argalen Keep, Eledhel, and Tol-Dhurath, alongside full quest, research/crafting, and player-trading systems. Login credentials and character records persist in a real backing MySQL database (RealmsLib) rather than flat player-save files, reflecting the engine's modern, service-oriented architecture.

libs.name: Final Realms
libs.english_description: A classic, from-scratch English-language MudOS mudlib whose own commit history dates to 1998 -- the oldest-vintage lib onboarded into this collection so far. A full game world, not a bare engine: character creation drops new arrivals into the "Hall of Creation," where a one-time `become <race>` command permanently picks one of 12 playable races (Drow, Duergar, Dwarf, Elf, Gnome, Goblin, Half-Elf, Half-Orc, Halfling, Human, Lizard-Man, Orc) before sending them to that race's own dedicated newbie zone -- real per-race taverns and shops, not a shared generic starting room. Five character guilds (Cleric, Fighter, Mage, Rogue, Warrior) round out the RPG progression, with the Mage guild alone branching into nine D&D-style specialist schools (Abjurer, Conjurer, Diviner, Enchanter, Illusionist, Invoker, Necromancer, Transmuter, and a general path), plus a full wizard-building toolset for creators.

libs.name: 泥潭三 / 《終極魔界》 (nitan3)
libs.english_description: A git-hosted snapshot of the same 'Nitan III' codebase already in this collection as nitan_san (archive-sourced) -- confirmed byte-identical across 15,235 of 15,236 shared files, including the master object. Branded in-game as 'Ultimate Demon Realm,' a skin over the shared NT/nitan/Lonely engine. New characters choose a name and personality and are delivered into the world by Pangu at the Valley of Life, matching the creation-myth path shared with nitan_san and nitan_ceshi. Needs no external database; registration and saves are local-file-based.

libs.name: 梦幻西游2002版
libs.english_description: A GitHub mirror of the same 2002-era "Qingdao Station" mhxy release already preserved in this project as mhxyqd -- confirmed byte-identical across all 14,563 files (including runtime state like adm/etc/wizlist), so no separate build was produced; see mhxyqd for the live, playable instance and its full fix catalog.

libs.name: 风云Ⅳ
libs.english_description: A GitHub mirror of the same "Fengyun IV" ("Wind and Cloud IV") codebase already preserved in this project as fengyun434 -- every file the two trees share is byte-identical; fengyun434's raw archive simply has ~100 extra files (backup .bak copies, board data, and accumulated player-residence save state) from being a later, lived-in snapshot of the same server. No separate build was produced; see fengyun434 for the live, playable instance and its full fix catalog.

libs.name: 金庸群侠传
libs.english_description: A GitHub mirror of the same 'jy' codebase already preserved in this project as jyqxc -- jyqxc's own raw archive ('金庸群侠传 (1).rar') extracts to a top-level directory literally named 'jy', and a full tree comparison against this clone found zero content differences across all 3,625 shared files (including a byte-identical adm/obj/master.c), with the only discrepancies being empty directories git does not track and a Windows binary distribution (driver.exe, MudOS.exe, etc.) that jyqxc's raw archive happened to include at its root. See jyqxc for the live, playable instance (port 40129) and its full fix catalog.

libs.archive: lpmuds.net/files/tmi2_fluffos_v3.zip, recovered via Wayback Machine 2026-08-25 (original site down)
libs.name: TMI-2
libs.english_description: A historically significant, widely-copied English-language LPMud mudlib from 1992-1996 whose std/ base classes, command-soul dispatch, and /adm/-rooted security-daemon layout were inherited by a large family of later mudlibs (this project's own catalog refers to a 'TMI-2/Falcon family' of descendants). This port is the 'famous TMI-2 quad' release itself: a landing zone with a general-purpose bulletin board, an Intermud-3 network-discussion room, a MudOS-driver-discussion room, a bug-report room, and a link down into /d/Fooland, plus the full TMI-2 wizard toolset (file/object inspection commands, the channel system, a student/teacher tutorial subsystem, FTP and HTTP daemons, and a resolv_str/resolv_ref scripting mini-language for wizard reference variables) and character creation across 13 playable races (dwarf, elf, gnome, human, orc, troll, halfling, sprite, shadow, ent, siren, skeleton, zombie). This collection's other TMI-2 1.4alpha-descended archive, mortremains, shares this lib's own credit line ("Truilkan@TMI"). Booting this lib also opens a real outbound connection to the public Intermud-3 router network, matching genuine upstream behavior rather than a bug.

What shipped and works: a real first-boot admin-setup installation wizard, full login/registration, security/privs access control, command dispatch, help, mail, message boards, and Intermud-3 networking, plus one small starting domain. Two optional example/teaching content trees included in the archive reference an incompatible, differently-named room/item API from a different snapshot of this engine and don't compile, so they're not playable content.

This is the most network-connected mud in the collection: it dials out to a live IMC2 hub and a separate Intermud-3 network on every boot, and even a bare, unattended boot triggers an automatic version-check that fetches the still-live dead-souls.net's release notes over a real HTTP connection.

Lennar Manor is a separate noble estate with its own reception hall, tea room, lower library, and barracks; Northern Wastes is a third, frozen area (furnace, freezer, void rooms) built on the same engine. A personal builder's workroom (realms/muirrum) holds several in-progress test rooms and abandoned editor scratch buffers -- a snapshot of a game still under active construction. Makes three real outbound network connections at boot (IMC2, Intermud-3, an automatic dead-souls.net RELEASE_NOTES fetch) -- do not sweep this lib into high-frequency automated re-boot loops.

One of the longest-running, most-studied LPMuds in existence (running continuously since 1991), set in Terry Pratchett's Discworld. New characters start in the famous circular Discworld Room in Ankh-Morpork's Cabbage Warehouse Rooming House, guided in by a wandering "womble" NPC. Uses a directory-based command dispatcher (a verb like `look` resolves to a file `cmds/living/l_ook.lpc`, the underscore marking its minimum abbreviation) layered under a `drunk_check()`/`lower_check()` eval-cost and command-queueing throttle.

New characters land in the central plaza of Gourd City (葫芦城中央广场), a hub with roads leading to four city gates, a bulletin board, and an NPC greeter. The world is organized into six domains -- gourd (the starting city), grid, pet, ship, special, and wiz -- and score displays a six-stat sheet (strength/wisdom/agility/willpower/constitution/luck) plus stamina and mana bars. Rather than a traditional wuxia master-disciple sect system, character progression runs through a profession office (职业介绍所) offering mage/warrior/priest classes, and further advancement is tied to a kingdom-building economy: players can construct a magic tower, training yard, or hero's guild once a kingdom accumulates enough gold and territory. A separate marriage/kinship system (swear/adopt/marry) handles social bonds instead of the genre's usual apprenticeship convention. libs.name: Sundering Shadows
libs.english_description: A long-running, still-live English-language fantasy LPMud built on a heavily customized Nightmare/TMI-lineage mudlib base -- 43,147 files (~47MB) that the live game auto-commits every 30 minutes. New characters emerge through a full command-driven, 15-stage creation wizard (class, gender, race, subrace, template, age, point-buy stat allocation, body type, hair/eye color, bonus languages, alignment, deity, class-special) before a scripted basic-commands tutorial drops them into the world proper. The std/races/ library lists 43 playable strains: the familiar human, elf, dwarf, gnome, halfling, half-elf, half-orc, and drow sit alongside centaurs, minotaurs, satyrs, dragonkin, wemics, kitsune, saurians, yuan-ti, firbolgs, gnolls, bugbears, and troll-kin, with a further tier -- devils, imps, devas, dragonkin, soulforged, strix -- locked behind account-level approval rather than open to every newcomer. Base classes offered at creation (fighter, thief, mage, cleric, druid, ranger, paladin, bard, barbarian, sorcerer, monk, warlock, psion, inquisitor, magus, cavalier, and more) are only the entry point: dozens of prestige classes are earned in play, from archmage, assassin, eldritch knight, and shadowdancer to hexblade, warmind, hierophant, and arcane trickster. The setting runs its own homegrown ten-deity pantheon -- Jarmila, Callamir, Kreysneothosies, Ryorik, Nilith, Lord Shadow, The Faceless One, Kismet, Lysara, and Nimnavanon, each with a distinct portfolio and alignment restrictions that gate which deities and class-special options a given character can take. The persistent world spans dozens of named zones built up over decades of individual-wizard development: the newbie cities of Tabor and Muuldaan, the city of Shadow with its own coliseum sparring grounds, an Underdark drow-and-derro tunnel network, a Ravenloft-flavored gothic-horror domain, a Mesoamerican-styled Atoyatl/Tecqumin jungle region with its own tabaxi denizens, the Dagger forest and marsh territories, plus dedicated guild halls, a magic college with its own demiplane, and player-run housing and shops.

libs.name: Nightmare Residuum
libs.english_description: A from-scratch space-themed LPMud that takes only its name and thematic inspiration from the classic Nightmare Mudlib, distinct from this collection's `nightmare3`/`nightmare4` in both codebase and setting. A new arrival wakes in Origin, a small orbital station (a central chamber with corridors to a tank room, a nanite-injection vendor, and a transporter) whose android greeter walks them through a two-stage character-creation process: first a species choice, then a "tank" console where `download <class>` installs one of six classes -- warrior, mystic, scoundrel, ranger, psionist, or paladin -- and `encode`/`randomize` sets physical attributes before `done` finalizes the specimen and releases it into the world. Leaving the station via Origin's transporter pad drops a character onto Planet, a fully procedural surface generated live from Perlin/simplex noise: every coordinate computes its own biome, heat, humidity, and elevation on the fly (tropical rainforest, desert, tundra, and more), populated with wildlife (curious raccoons, feral cats, large ants, lurking vultures, plasma snails, rabid rats, watchful crows, wild dogs) to hunt or be hunted by. Architecturally the mudlib runs a genuine account/character split -- one login account can hold several independent characters, each with its own save file and its own class/level/stats/experience/defeat-count progression -- and drives its whole verb/command/ability layer through a custom dispatch registry rather than the driver's native `add_action()`. The very first character ever created on a fresh copy of the world is automatically granted immortal rank. The codebase ships its own in-game unit-test and code-coverage framework (`D_TEST`, invoked live via a `test` command) directly alongside the game content. English-language content.

Unlike the wuxia combat-focused Simplified-Chinese family that dominates most of this collection, RevivalWorld is an economic-simulation and city-building game with English-named content throughout (areas, cities, and quest chains such as a 'Suphia and Benjamin' storyline): players occupy land, found cities and governments, build houses, shops, and warehouses, and progress through an agricultural-then-industrial-then-knowledge-era production chain, trading the results on an in-game stock market. New characters start at the Wizard Temple and choose a city to settle in via the gocity system. Boot renders a full HTML world map, and a real intermud2 daemon exchanges startup/mudlist broadcasts with other MUDs on the public internet.

libs.name: LPmud 1.4.1-A
libs.english_description: A small, genuinely historical LPMud reference world -- "HMC LP-mud" (Harvey Mudd College), version 1.4.1-A, bundled with its own classic C-language LPMud driver (the mudlib content here runs under this project's own FluffOS build instead). A university-account game, not a commercial title: new characters arrive in the Endoplasmatorium ("a place where people without bodies come to get them") next to a clinic, a village green, and an elevator connecting up to the wizards' hall. The Adventurers' Guild runs a classic experience-and-gold leveling ladder with twenty title ranks, from "the utter novice" up through journeyman/master magician and sorcerer tiers to "the apprentice Wizard". Beyond the village (green, road, shore, bank, pub, church, and a general store) lies a real overworld: a ten-room forest chain, a mountain pass and peak, a giant's lair and treasure path, a sea and sea floor, and a chain of thirteen numbered planar rooms. A soul-verb social/emote command set (`smile`, etc.) and basic wizard tooling round out the toolkit. The game world is deliberately small and thin -- a real early-1990s single-author teaching project, not an omission in this port.

libs.name: Arkadia
libs.english_description: A Polish-language localization of the Genesis/CD-driver mudlib engine family -- this collection's already-onboarded libs/genesis is the English original -- and its first non-Chinese/non-English-language entry. A standard fantasy setting in the CD-driver mold, with the localization's own distinctive twist on character creation: a new arrival must type out all six Polish grammatical cases of their own name (mianownik/dopelniacz/celownik/biernik/narzednik/miejscownik), checked for validity and re-confirmable during the first six hours of play, since other players' commands need to grammatically decline a target's name correctly. The standard English soul commands are fully replaced by Polish equivalents throughout -- spojrz/sp to look, zakoncz to quit, stan for a status/score sheet, nagraj to save, haslo to change password -- so play reads as a genuinely Polish game rather than a translated skin over English verbs. A freshly-registered soul arrives as a formless spirit in a circular stone hall ringed by five silent statues, each holding a torch that casts the only light in the room, with a strange portal standing at the room's center and a passage leading off through the one flat wall; the intent is to touch a statue to choose a race, then step through the portal to be given a body and truly enter the world. As shipped, that final step never fires -- no path in the hall actually completes the transition -- so a new soul can register, log back in across sessions, and use ghost-level commands like looking around and checking status, but never leaves that spectral, disembodied state through ordinary play; combat, shops, and guild training all sit on the far side of a threshold nothing in-game currently opens.

libs.name: OpenLib
libs.english_description: A real MudOS v22.1a6-era mudlib (formerly "UltraLib") by Tim McIntosh, released as a single alpha snapshot (v0.1) in late 1996 before development ceased -- genuinely distinct from every other lib in this collection: a from-scratch English-language codebase built around a UNIX-flavored security and shell model rather than the usual Chinese-wuxia lineage. Login bootstraps by connecting as the literal username "root" (a privileged bootstrap account defined in security.h), then uses in-game commands (mkwiz/addmem/chmem) to promote a real admin character before retiring root's own privileges. Access control is entirely privilege-based (a custom D_ACCESS-style security_d.lpc consulting per-directory read/write protection tables walked up the path hierarchy) with no driver uid usage at all. Players get a real UNIX-like shell (nmsh, a "new mud shell" supporting cd/pwd/pushd/popd/aliases/history) as their command interpreter rather than a flat verb table, and the archive ships a working FTP daemon, finger daemon, and HTTP daemon as real listening services alongside the game itself. The shipped content is deliberately minimal (GETTING_STARTED admits "the lib is incomplete") -- a single starting room at the exact center of the mudlib's universe with two exits, and a handful of unfinished example object classes (a generic shop, money, a zombie) that reference the original author's own never-shipped personal test items under his own /u/ wizard directory. English-language content throughout.

libs.name: Foundation I
libs.english_description: A stripped-down, classic Nightmare-3.3-derived LPC library released by George Reese ("Descartes of Borg") in April 1995 -- a bare engine (login/registration, security, command dispatch, help, mail, message boards, Intermud-3) with no combat, limbs, or stats system at all, meant as a clean base for LPC programmers to build their own game on top of, not a playable-out-of-the-box world. This is the direct, earlier ancestor of this collection's separate `foundation2` (a distinct, more developed later release by the same author) -- not a duplicate. The one shipped starting room is a softly-lit cavern with magic pools, with the real player command set (look/status/inventory/quit and more) fully implemented. An optional teaching content tree references an incompatible room/item API from a different snapshot of this engine and doesn't compile, a pre-existing content mismatch. Like foundation2, this lib makes a real outbound Intermud-3 socket connection at boot (to a near-certainly-defunct 1990s host) and should not be swept into high-frequency automated re-boot loops.

libs.name: Haven
libs.english_description: A long-running, genuinely large Dead Souls/Nightmare-lineage production game self-titled 'Haven,' set in the world of Kailie -- 13,589 source files (7,328 under domains/ alone), not a near-stock demo like this collection's sibling dshakkard. New characters begin 'in the skies above Kailie,' a staging room where reading a newbie book awards a real quest completion before descending into one of several playable hometowns. Kailie has its own pantheon (the Lord of Balance Duuktsaryth, and the Primal Gods Amelia, Balishae, Syra, Morgoth, Zaxan, and Ahriman), a creation-myth timeline, and its own calendar counting years from Haven's own founding. Playable races span humans, elves, dwarves, half-elves, orcs, half-orcs, sprites, skaven, lamrani, dark-elves, and wild-elves, with goblins, kobolds, gelflings, nosferatu, drughkor, and meuzzin appearing as lore/NPC races. 21 custom domains make up the live world -- averath, baria, crystal_reaches, estergrym, frostmarches, gurov, havenwood, innersea, islands, namatar, peninsula, southern_coast, tairi, valley, westwood, xandria, and yozrath among them -- towns, wilderness, and dungeons built up over years of individual wizards' work, plus a marriage/chapel system, player estates, a crafting subsystem, an in-game newsgroup daemon, and a wizard FTP daemon. 25 personal wizard workrooms sit under realms/ (Duuk, Zaxan, Mahkefel, Alessandra, Laoise, Torak, and others), several holding real in-progress building projects alongside old scratch files. Makes a real outbound Intermud-3 connection on boot.

libs.name: SluggyMUD
libs.english_description: A bare, unfinished LPC mudlib skeleton whose own two-line README states it is 'a component-based mudlib designed to run on the FluffOS LPC driver.' A single 2013 commit, root at lib/{core,public,secure}: a real, permissive master.lpc/valid.lpc pair (get_root_uid/get_bb_uid/creator_file/valid_read/valid_write/valid_override all present) and a real simul_efun.lpc, but genuinely no game content at all -- public/domains, every lib/{component,obj,daemon,single} directory under all three of core/public/secure, and core/cmds are all empty placeholders, there is no room/environment system (the void singleton is a one-line stub), and login.lpc's own comment admits it 'needs fixed to handle passwords' (every connection becomes an anonymous, passwordless identity). What's real: a handful of dev commands (who, say, eval, ed, rm, update, dest, quit, shutdown, plus the hidden, non-advertised speed benchmark and tests self-test runner) and, once repaired, a genuinely substantial ~113-file compiler/efun self-test suite. The bare recursive `tests` walk correctly surfaces one genuine, interesting compiler-behavior difference -- a 'should fail to compile' fixture that actually compiles fine on this build -- and stops there by the suite's own intentional design, rather than continuing silently. One pre-existing, left-undocumented content gap: the login banner advertises an `efun` command that was never implemented anywhere in the shipped source. No outbound network side effects.

libs.name: Wilderness
libs.english_description: A production game built on the LIMA mudlib framework (v1.0a9) -- the same natural-language-parser, capability-security, wizard-Unix-shell codebase already onboarded standalone as libs/lima -- but an independent, much older (May 2000) snapshot with the framework's own AUTO_WIZ demo shortcut disabled, so real characters start as ordinary mortals rather than instant wizards. New characters float in 'The Void,' whose own room text describes an inky blackness where 'a wispy tendril of smoke will waft by your face' before a circular portal that always stays fixed in front of you; stepping through it drops you into a wizard-built area such as /wiz/branin/workroom, 'a swirling maelstrom of color' with a meeping snake inside. Beyond the entry point, the built world spans a labyrinth, caves, a beach, an attic with two Beavis-and-Butthead-style easter-egg NPCs, a cult area with its own foyer and portal, and dozens of individually-built rooms and objects -- a sword in a stone, a bungee jump, a car wash, a working camera/photograph system, guild-guard NPCs. Character creation is an 8-attribute point-buy stat allocation plus a size choice and a short personality quiz, on top of the LIMA framework's centralized natural-language command parser, capability-based security daemon, wizard Unix-like shells, Intermud-3 support, and a modular combat system (death/health/wield/armor/pulse/blows/formula/advancement submodules). Shares Harvey Mudd College academic hosting (cs.hmc.edu) with this collection's libs/lpmud141, though it's an unrelated, much newer (MudOS v22.2-era) codebase -- unlike lpmud141, which required a from-scratch master-object reconstruction.

libs.name: Majik 4
libs.english_description: A 1998-1999 hobbyist mudlib by Finnish author Tero Ilkka Leino ("namhas"), the fourth incarnation of his Majik project and a sharp architectural break from majik3 (also in this collection): instead of room objects, the whole game world is a real 2D grid rendered by a dedicated graphical client, driven over a custom binary-framed wire protocol rather than plain telnet. A fresh character rolls a race (human, elf, orc, troll, or dwarf) and lands in Hilltop Village -- a hand-built little town of named locations (a bank, a post office, a general store, the Hilltop Inn, an "Intersection," and a hilltop shrine called the Legendary Hilltop of the Gods with a nearby Plaque of Explorers) populated by a banker, grocer, innkeeper, guard, and a hermit NPC forever muttering about the application he's filling out to become a wizard "greater than Namhas itself" -- a wink at the author's own handle. West of the village lies Bral Gaur, a dwarven area named and lettered in Gwel, an invented dwarven conlang with its own noun/verb/adjective word lists bundled in the archive. The project's own README candidly admits development stopped while the engine was "almost, still not even beta," before the team moved on to a planned 3D successor (majik3d) that was never released -- so wilderness beyond the two hand-authored areas is thin, and the terrain generator that would have filled it in was never finished as portable code. See also majik3, the same author's 1997-1998 predecessor project.

(Potential Psychic Energy) resource on the HUD and score sheet alongside HP/SP, a custom greathorneddragon race alongside the stock dwarf/elf/human set, and 'universal credits' as the town's currency. The town hub has Horace's General Supply Shop, the First Village Bank (with Zoe the bank teller), a Healer's Guild selling remedies, and a talking beggar on Saquivor Road who hands new arrivals a real map item. The repo itself is a genuine slice of someone's personal, in-progress mud rather than a finished release or a pristine archive -- it arrived with three live wizard accounts (gravity, thurtea, shrub) already in play and only ten total upstream commits, the last few just balancing tweaks ('multiple fixes credits added mana now ppe'). Its most striking piece of content, though, doesn't work: domains/omega is 150 files describing a detailed multi-floor sci-fi space station ('Omega Station') with NPCs, a shop, and an elevator, backed by a further 33-file domains/common item/ship library -- but every file in both trees inherits base classes (LIVING, M_VENDOR, ARMOUR, ELEVATOR, and more) that are never defined anywhere in the repository, so none of it compiles or loads; the author's own half-built compat.h shim shows they were actively working toward supporting it before development stopped. The bundled domains/std Lima-style builder-school example area (315 files, stock to Dead Souls 3.9 itself) hits the identical missing-framework problem.

libs.name: DarkeLIB
libs.english_description: The real, original DarkeLIB circa 1999 ("Daybreak Ridge"), a from-scratch English-language Lima/Nightmare/TMI-lineage MudOS mudlib -- the actual ancestor codebase this project's already-onboarded rifts2 (RiftsMUD2) later forked into a Rifts-setting reskin. This fork (thraeq/DarkeLIB) is the community-maintained, more actively FluffOS-adapted branch, carrying two decades (1999-2018) of real hand-built areas rather than a stock demo. The world's own creation myth (Drizzt's bundled HISTORY document) opens with a solitary god called the Demiurge abandoning an imperfect creation to a struggle between Ethereals and Elves that eventually produces every playable race -- Humans, Dwarves, Gnomes, Orcs, Trolls, Sprites, Wood-Elves -- through slavery, experimentation, and a world-shaping Great War. Individual zones build on that backdrop with their own micro-lore: the Village of Nalon (arm_dealers) is a monastery of hand-to-hand and mind-discipline monks founded by a war-weary pacifist warrior; Illuminarae's mansion sits on ground poisoned by an elven bio-weapon that went catastrophically wrong on its own makers; the Nocte Undead Grounds are a canyon-and-tunnel necropolis of skeletons, ghouls, and bandits; Damned runs a set of named story quests (recovering a lich-stolen soul for the adventurer Rufus Tenderfoot, a stolen Dead Rose, a missing emerald) rather than generic fetch tasks; and further zones (drizzt, khojem, warsyn, zortek, shadowraith, soulslayer, excelsior, diewarzau) add their own wizard-authored dungeons, spell lines, and boss fights on top.

libs.name: Spacemud
libs.english_description: A space-themed fork of the LIMA Mudlib (the same FluffOS reference framework already onboarded standalone as libs/lima) that keeps Lima's engine -- natural-language command parsing ('take the red potion from the box'), capability-based security, Unix-like wizard shell -- but swaps its fantasy wizard's-guildhall demo world for a decaying, nine-floor space station called Omega. A fresh character wakes up there and can wander its maintenance corridors, waiting rooms, and a domed Stargate Terminal (a pulsating circular teleport platform under a star-filled skylight) run by chief landing controller Aria Voss and a small cast of named station staff (Doc Green, Doc Williams, Rigel Fluxx, Zara Nebulon, Max Nova); the Yakitori delivery guild runs its own chef/cashier counter selling skewer snacks, tech gremlins and space roaches skitter the lower decks, and a lunar lurker mob and salvageable hyperspace hoodie armour round out Omega's authored content. Underneath the station sits a from-scratch procedural-universe layer (space_d/ship_d/spacestation_d/proc_gen_d) that generates star systems and planets at first boot -- Greek-alphabet naming conventions, gravity/mass/radius stats -- meant to support the game's real ambition per its own README: fly a purchased spacecraft, haul and sell goods, dock at stations, and eventually manage planet-side corporations, layered on top of a genuine crafting/salvage system (break weapons and armour into scrap metal, cloth, and plastics at any workbench). The parallel domains/pinto directory is not spacemud's own content -- it's LimaLib's official docs.limalib.dev tutorial reference code (a single swamp room and a swan NPC), bundled for readers following the upstream learning path rather than a second game area. First character auto-granted wizard/admin per Lima's own documented AUTO_WIZ convention.

libs.name: Holy Mission
libs.english_description: A large (~24,000 .lpc file), heavily player-authored MudOS-lineage fantasy world originally run out of Linz, Austria (the login banner reads 'Welcome to the Holy Mission at Linz, Austria'). Character creation is a straight race pick across seven Tolkien-flavored races -- human, elf, half-elf, dwarf, hobbit, orc, and troll -- each with its own short lore blurb straight from the archive's own doc/races files (hobbits explicitly called out as natural thieves for their agility, orcs as 'usually an evil race' but not fixed-alignment, trolls as large, slow, inately-evil brutes), feeding into five class guilds each split into three sub-specializations: priest (druid/shaman/monk), adventurer (ranger/vagabond/jedi), mage (fire/water/earth/air elemental), fighter (barbarian/berserker/samurai), and thief (pirate/ninja/assassin). The adventurers' guild runs a real fetch quest ('Retrieve the Orc slayer from the evil orc shaman, and give it to Leo'). The starting village radiates out from a church consecrated to 'Illuvatar' (a direct Tolkien reference) that revives the dead at its own altar, with a churchyard, sewers, a guard house, bank, shops, and the guildhouse nearby, plus a separate orc valley, forest, mines, and a whole distinct 'south' region -- extensive player/wizard-authored content built up over years of individual work (the archive's own comments date from the early-to-mid 1990s onward).

libs.name: Basis
libs.english_description: A small, historically significant 1993 English-language LPMud mudlib by John Garnett ("Truilkan", also the author of the already-onboarded tmi2/TMI-2, but this is an earlier, deliberately smaller project). A thin core-infrastructure sketch rather than a game: a two-room test area, a working registration/login flow, and a real bin/-command dispatch tree, but no quests, combat, or score command. Basis's std/ base classes, groups/access permission model, and bin command-dispatch system were later inherited by TMI-2 itself.

libs.name: LPmud 2.4.5
libs.english_description: A pristine, pre-LDMud LPMud 2.4.5 snapshot -- the mudlib distributed with Lars Pensjo's own original LPMud driver line, from right before the LDMud/MudOS fork. A real, playable small world (286 files, hundreds of rooms) rather than an infrastructure sketch: new characters land in the village church (which hides a call-button-summoned elevator behind its west wall) and can explore a green, market road, bank, shops, and an adventurers' guild that runs a real fetch quest -- 'Retrieve the Orc slayer from the evil orc shaman, and give it to Leo' -- pointing players at an orc valley with its own orc-treasure room. A twelve-room forest and a 29-tunnel mine flank the village; a giant's lair, path, and confrontation room house a cloned, aggressive level-15 giant NPC; and the village shore road leads out to an entirely separate 'south' region -- its own self-contained ~49-room forest, 18-room island archipelago, and 30-room shoreline.

libs.name: LPlib8
libs.english_description: An experimental mudlib written by Lars Pensjo himself -- LPMud's original creator -- as his own testbed for the new features of 'LPmud game driver 3.0', explicitly not the well-known CDlib for Genesis. 54 files, structurally more modern than sibling archives (real inherit throughout, create() already the primary constructor).

libs.name: MiniMud
libs.english_description: A genuine pre-LDMud, Amylaar-driver-era testbed skeleton -- only 19 files (7 commands, one room, one player class, master + simul_efun). Not a game, a driver-feature demo: register with a bare name (no password), one starting room, look/say/who/ls, plus two wizard debug tools (eval -- compile and run an arbitrary LPC expression on the spot; update -- destruct and reload a single object).

libs.name: The Brass Ring
libs.english_description: A Dead Souls 3.8.x-based game-in-development (self-titled 'The Brass Ring') that ships as a content overlay for Dead Souls rather than a full mudlib on its own. On top of the underlying Dead Souls engine, TBR bundles a full DikuMud Alfa port (domains/diku-alfa/, 1185 files -- Midgaard and its zones) and is actively building its own bespoke fantasy continent, Etnar (the village of Wyr, with NPCs Albert Derby/Waltin Kelley/Caltan Dowini/the Pierce family already in place and a virtual wilderness room system). Character creation includes an age gate, a screen-reader accessibility question, an 8-race pick, and a complete 6/4/4 primary/secondary/minor skill selection across all 28 skills; new characters enter play in Saquivor, the real starting town (distinct from the tutorial start room), from which Etnar's Wyr (The Lounge) and diku-alfa's Temple of Midgaard are both reachable. No outbound network connections at boot -- unlike several sibling Dead-Souls-family libs, this one is safe for high-frequency automated re-boot loops.

libs.name: Dock 9
libs.english_description: A small English-language LPC mudlib built on the same LPUniversity/Sapidlib teaching-engine base as this project's lpuni -- a full login/registration/security/command-dispatch/help/mail/news/channel/Intermud-3 engine, with a small but genuinely original starting area: the dock town of Trepi, an island city trading across the Trepi Strait with Nulens, a 'relatively recently discovered continent' now being colonized by the empires of Erplak, an old continent from beyond the Besling Ocean. New characters start on Dock 9 itself -- 'one of the more magical places on the world,' where 'for as long as anyone can recall, people have appeared, lost and confused' -- among a network of numbered docks (7, 8, 10, 11, 12) connected by piers, cargo warehouses, and a customs house. A helpful greeter-sailor NPC welcomes each new arrival by name and, on request, teleports them to a separate floating-island training area (Make); a second, wandering 'unsteady sailor' NPC demonstrates subdomain wandering while visibly drunk on Nulens's lax law enforcement, name-dropping a place called Calliet. There is no combat/stats system at all. Also makes a real outbound Intermud-3 network connection at boot, same as lpuni/imud/tmi2/skylib.
